Lessons.Title: Symmetry in Figures (Part 1)
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will introduce the concept of line symmetry and for you to identify lines of symmetry in two-dimensional figures.
This lesson introduces you to symmetry as an attribute of two-dimensional figures. You relate lines of symmetry to the lines of folding that create two identical halves: if a figure is folded along or mirrored across such a line, the two halves would overlap and match exactly. The idea of folding along or mirroring across a line is essential here, as there are some figures that could be decomposed into two identical halves but have no line symmetry.

2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up: Notice and Wonder: Seeing Double (10 minutes); Activity 1: Perfect Matches (20 minutes); Activity 2: In Search of Symmetry (15 minutes); Activity 3: Just Keep Folding [OPTIONAL] (10 minutes); Cool-down: One Line or More than One? (5 minutes)
Source-goal geometric reasoning: A line of symmetry divides a figure into two reflected matching halves; a fold tests correspondence.

Edulytics worked explanation: Fold or imagine folding the actual given paper figure along the proposed line. Compare the resulting halves: matching edges and corners indicate symmetry. Count distinct valid folding axes, not just lines passing through the center.
First-party Edulytics Cool-down (not gated original): How many lines of symmetry does a non-square rectangle have?
Original student diagrams, teacher card sorting, paper folding, and physical drawings require figure-by-figure / teacher validation.
